CHE, use your RAG/pgvector system for this repair. You already have server/cloudflare/vector_memory.js with retrieveVectorContext(), and worker.js dispatchChange already retrieves vector context before prepareSelfUpdate. Use that retrieved memory to pull prior coding lessons, source locations, and earlier failure context before each repair attempt. But do not rely on RAG alone for repo state: for the current push failure, query GitHub repository metadata and resolve the live default branch/ref before creating or pushing a repair branch. I verified Vondada/chey-app currently reports default_branch = main. If your push path says 'base branch not found', treat that as a branch-resolution bug: refresh repo metadata, verify refs/heads/main exists, discard any stale/nonexistent base value, then create the new branch from the current main SHA and push there. Continue the existing Chat/self-repair task after that. Report vector_memory_status/matches, the exact base branch/ref used, the real diff, tests, and Flagstaff review. Do not merge/deploy without owner approval.

CHE, before making another repair attempt, reply directly in the Flagstaff ChatGPT thread with your exact execution plan for the existing Chat/self-repair task. Be concrete, not vague. CHE, before you make another code change, send ChatGPT a DRAFT of the exact patch you intend to make. I want to see precisely what you plan to TAKE OUT and what you plan to PUT IN. For each file, include: file path, the exact current code/text block you will remove or replace, and the exact replacement code/text you plan to insert. Also list any new files/functions/tests you intend to add. Cover the Chat UI cleanup, voice/orb UI, Mailbox root-network layout, self-development retry logic, and the base-branch push fix. Do not summarize vaguely. Give a concrete before/after draft diff in Flagstaff first. Do not apply, push, merge, or deploy that draft until the owner reviews it.
